abstract: D-Cinema content is extremely valuable and, as a result, protecting it requires a combination of cryptographic security, physical security, and forensic auditing tools. Such a level of security need not, however, come at the expense of interoperability, reliability, and usability. To enable interoperability, the SMPTE DC28 committee has been leading an effort to standardize a D-Cinema content protection architecture using input from a broad spectrum of industry participants. While some aspects of the architecture, such as device registries, remain under consideration, its core components are now worldwide standards, being actively implemented by manufacturers, content providers, service providers, and exhibitors alike.

authors.bio: Pierre-Anthony Lemieux has been involved in D-cinema standards since the early days of the SMPTE DC28 Technology Committee. He currently chairs its Security/Key Management Ad Hoc Group and previously co-chaired the DC28.4 Study Group on Content Protection & Conditional Access. He is director of Technology Strategy at Dolby Laboratories, where he focuses on standards and business development for cinema and consumer applications. He received a PhD degree from the University of California in Los Angeles and a BSc from McGill University.
